□音
成化十四年三月十□日，太子少保禮部尚書臣鄒榦等於天門奏為科舉事：「會試天下舉人，取中三百五十名。本年三月十五日殿試，合請讀卷官及執事等官，太子少保吏部尚書兼謹身殿大學士萬安等五十二員。其進士出身等第，恭依高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。」奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

translation_en:
Record of the Jinshi Graduates of the Year □□□□ [title partly illegible: 登□錄].
□音 [heading partly illegible; meaning uncertain].
On the tenth or a subsequent day [十□; final digit illegible] of the third month of the fourteenth year of Chenghua (1478), your servant Zou Gan, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Rites, and others submitted a memorial at Tianmen [?] concerning the civil-service examinations: “In the Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates (juren) from throughout the realm, 350 candidates were selected. For the Palace Examination on the fifteenth day of the third month of this year, we request the appointment of readers and other officiating personnel: Wan An, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall, and others, totaling fifty-two officials. As for the classes of jinshi status to be conferred, we respectfully follow the qualifications imperially prescribed by Emperor Gao: the first class customarily comprises three men. The first receives the lower sixth rank, and the second and third receive the upper seventh rank; they are granted jinshi with honors. Those in the second class receive the lower seventh rank and are granted regular jinshi status. Those in the third class receive the upper eighth rank and are granted associate jinshi status.” The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respectfully received.
Readers
Wan An, Grand Master for Assisting in Governance, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall. 〔Jinshi of the wuchen year (1448).〕
Liu Xu, [four illegible characters], Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Revenue, and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion. 〔Jinshi of the wuchen year (1448).〕
Liu Ji, [four illegible characters], Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion. 〔Jinshi of the wuchen year (1448).〕

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month in the fourteenth year of Chenghua (1478), the tribute scholars went to the inner palace and sat the examination in □tian Hall [?]. They were presented with an imperially bestowed policy question.

On the morning of the seventeenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in their court robes. [Two illegible characters.] The Embroidered-Uniform Guard arranged the ceremonial regalia on the vermilion steps and within the vermilion courtyard. [Illegible passage.] At □tian Hall [?], officials of the Court of State Ceremonial announced the names [?]. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow results placard, led by drums and music, out through Chang'an Left Gate. After the placard had been posted outside the gate, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.

On the eighteenth day of the third month…

陸釴〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣，官籍，國子生，治易經，字惟立，行八，年四十三，七月初七日生〕。曾祖浩卿，祖八疇，父自德〔倉副使，贈編脩〕，母張氏〔封太孺人〕。永感下，兄守陳〔侍講學士〕，弟守隅。娶全氏。浙江鄉試第一名，會試第四名。

曾追〔貫江西吉安府泰和縣，儒籍，國子生，治書經，字文甫，行二，年三十六，四月二十日生〕。曾祖伯高〔贈編脩〕，祖鶴齡〔侍講學士〕，父蒙簡〔茶馬大使〕，母陳氏〔封孺人〕。慈侍下，兄道甫，弟迥、遙、退。娶陳氏。江西鄉試第四十九名，會試第五十五名。
translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the distinction of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi).

Yin Zhi, courtesy name Shimei, was registered in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged fifty-four, born on the seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wensheng, his grandfather Huanzong, and his father Guangxiang; his father’s former wife was née Yin, and his mother was née Xiao. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Ping, Xuezhun, Xuan, and Shao. He married a woman née Xiao and subsequently a woman née Wu. He placed ninetieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Yi, courtesy name Weili, was registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in an official household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked eighth among his brothers and was aged forty-three, born on the seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Haoqing, his grandfather Bachou, and his father Zide, a Granary Vice Commissioner posthumously granted the title of Compiler; his mother, née Zhang, was granted the title of Grand Dame (ta孺ren, tai ruren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Shouchen was an Expositor-in-waiting, and his younger brother was Shouyu. He married a woman née Quan. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Zhui [?], courtesy name Wenfu, was registered in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a scholarly household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the twentieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Bogao was posthumously granted the title of Compiler; his grandfather Heling was an Expositor-in-waiting; and his father Mengjian was a Commissioner of a Tea and Horse Office. His mother, née Chen, was granted the title of Dame (ruren). His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Daofu, and his younger brothers were Jiong, Yao, and Tui. He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second class: 110 men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Liang Chu was registered in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shuhou; he was third in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the eleventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Chucai, his grandfather Zhiqing, and his father Zushun; his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. He had an elder brother whose name is illegible and younger brothers Fang, Dian, and Yi. His wife was née Feng. His rank in the Guangdong Provincial Examination is partly illegible (第十□名); he ranked first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Xiong was registered with the Yulin (Imperial Bodyguard) [remainder of registration illegible; ?] and was a native of Renhe County. He was a student of the Shuntian Prefectural School and specialized in the Classic of Rites [following text illegible; ?]. He was thirty years old and was born on the seventeenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yin, his grandfather’s name is illegible, and his father was Chun; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Yan. He ranked 102nd in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Hao was registered in Taiping County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military household. An additional student of the county school, he specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Shiwen; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the tenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Shizhou, his grandfather Shangwan, and his father Tong, a student of the Directorate of Education; his mother was née Lin. The statement concerning his parents’ survival is illegible [?]. He had a younger brother, Jie, and his wife was née Zhong. He ranked sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

His courtesy name was Jizhi; he ranked first among his brothers, was forty-seven years old, and was born on the sixteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Guang, his grandfather Gen, his father Yong, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Fuzeng. He married a woman née Cheng and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Kejing, his grandfather Cong, his father Mingshan, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, and his mother née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhenzhi and Maozhi, and his wife was née Wan. He placed twenty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His father’s former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Cui. The statement of his parents’ survival is illegible [?]. □ Cong (surname illegible), courtesy name Runfu, was registered in a civilian household in Anren County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. An additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuyun; his grandfather, Zheng, was an Assistant Prefect; his father was Mian; and his mother was Lady □ (surname illegible). Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qi, Pu, and Yu, and he married Lady Hua. He placed fifty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 301st in the Metropolitan Examination.

An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Haoren, his grandfather Jun, his father Bin, and his mother Lady He. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhang and Lu, and he married Lady Wei. He placed seventy-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Ke, courtesy name Yingkui, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bocheng; his grandfather, Renyu, was posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Ji, was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, posthumously granted the title of Surveillance Commissioner; and his mother, Lady Xiong, was invested with the title Lady of Peace (anren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Zhi, and he married Lady Hu. He placed 116th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 327th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Qin, courtesy name Jingzhi, was registered in an artisan household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a native of Changzhou County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twelfth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Jing□ (name partly illegible), was posthumously granted the title of Office Manager; his grandfather was Suiliang, his father Mao, his mother Lady Yu, and his stepmother Lady Lin. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married Lady □ (surname illegible). He placed 107th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

楊傑〔貫山西太原府平定州軍籍，國子生，治書經，字廷俊，行四，年三十五，八月初五日生〕。曾祖叔誠，祖玘〔通判〕，父宗灝，前母荆氏，母王氏。慈侍下，兄英〔貢士〕、華，娶黄氏。山西鄉試第六名，會試第九十名。

從時〔貫四川成都後衛軍籍，重慶府巴縣人，國子生，治書經，字用中，行九，年三十六，二月二十六日生〕。曾祖士興〔典史〕，祖文通，父思永，前母何氏、陳氏，母黄氏。□□下，弟榮、英、良、宣、貫、衣、寧，娶韋氏，繼娶孫氏。□□□□三十八名，會試第七名。
translation_en:
Zeng Yuan, registered in a civilian household in Luling County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Benshen; he ranked second among his brothers and was forty-one years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zikui, his grandfather Sigao, and his father Yanxun; his mother was Lady □. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Che, and he married Lady Xiao. He placed seventeenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Qiong, registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuru; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the sixteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather □fu, and his father Mengshan; his mother was Lady Qian. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Gui, and he married Lady Yan. He placed eleventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Jie, registered in a military household in Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tingjun; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Shucheng, his grandfather Qi (an Assistant Prefect), and his father Zonghao. His father’s former wife was Lady Jing, and his mother was Lady Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Ying (a tribute scholar, gongshi) and Hua; he married Lady Huang. He placed sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cong Shi, registered in a military household of the Chengdu Rear Guard in Sichuan and a native of Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yongzhong; he ranked ninth among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Shixing (a County Clerk), his grandfather Wentong, and his father Siyong. His father’s former wives were Lady He and Lady Chen, and his mother was Lady Huang. The statement of his parents’ survival is illegible [?]. His younger brothers were Rong, Ying, Liang, Xuan, Guan, Yi, and Ning [name readings and division uncertain]. He married Lady Wei and subsequently Lady Sun. He placed thirty-eighth in an examination whose designation is illegible [?], and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan □ 衍□ [?], courtesy name Shiyan, was registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fifth in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the nineteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongyi; his grandfather, Shida; his father, Zhi, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother, née □. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Fan and □, and he married a woman née Yao. He placed eighty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Xiang 蔡相, courtesy name Yuanding, was registered in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, in an artisan household. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-two, and born on the twenty-third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Liang; his grandfather, Run, granted the title of Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works; his father, Zhi, an Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right; and his mother, née Tu, granted the title of Lady of Suitability. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Shi, Cuo, and Yi, and he married a woman née Yang. He placed 119th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ji 劉紀, courtesy name Zhenzhi, was registered in Mianzhu County, Hanzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Pusheng; his grandfather, Gui; his father, Huai; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Gang, and he married a woman née Cheng. He placed fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zhi 劉質, courtesy name Yuebin, was registered in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was ninth in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather's name is illegible; his grandfather was Bochong, an Assistant Prefect; his father, Jiabi; and his mother, née □. The statement concerning his surviving parents or grandparents is illegible [?]. His elder brothers were Chao and Zheng; the younger brother or brothers' names are illegible [?]. He married a woman whose surname is illegible. His Provincial Examination location and full rank are illegible; the surviving rank text reads “twelve” [?]. He placed eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang Zhao 黃昭 was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian; the two opening characters are illegible [?]. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shouyu, and he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, born on the fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Renshizhan [?]; his grandfather, Yangbao, was an Erudite of the National University; his father, Jing, was a Station Master; and his mother’s surname is illegible. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman surnamed Lin. He placed second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Gang 張綱 was registered in a military household in Lai’an County, Chuzhou, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Wanshan, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shanxiu, his grandfather Menghe, his father Fu, and his mother a woman surnamed Lü. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Jin and Shen. He married a woman surnamed Feng. He placed 102nd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ao Shan 敖山 was registered in a military household in Shen County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jingzhi, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, born on the seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Lin, his father Xian, and his mother a woman surnamed Cui, officially honored as a chaste widow. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Song. He married a woman surnamed Gui. He placed first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Si Zhen 巳振 [?] was registered in a military household in Neihuang County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wensheng, and he was first in birth order, aged twenty-four, born on the □一 day of the second month [date partly illegible]. His great-grandfather was Da, his grandfather Bin, his father Hao, and his mother a woman surnamed Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Lun, Zhuo, and Ze. He married a woman surnamed Song. He placed 100th in the Provincial Examination for an illegible jurisdiction and 24□th in the Metropolitan Examination [final digit illegible].

translation_en:
Xu You 徐佑, registered in Suning County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached government-school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yunji; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the twenty-first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Deyue; his grandfather, Fu, and father, Yan, were both former Investigating Censors. His mother, née Ba [?], had been granted the title Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jun, Xin, Jia, and Yu, and his wife was née Song. He placed fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Lian 劉濂, registered in Linqing County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zongzhou; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yifu, his grandfather Gongzhi, and his father Rui. His father's principal wife was née Bu [?], and his birth mother was née Han. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yan, his younger brothers were Han and Yuan, and his wife was née Song. He placed sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Tai 蔣泰, registered in Jiande County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Daoheng; he ranked fourteenth in the family birth order, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the twenty-third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongliang, his grandfather Shuqing, and his father Zongyu. His mother was née Zhou and his stepmother née Xu. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Hou, his younger brother Liang, and his wife was née He. He placed seventy-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zhong 劉忠, registered in Chenliu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Sizhi; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the twelfth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Qian, his grandfather Heng, and his father Da, an Instructor at the National University. His mother's surname is illegible (□). Both parents were living. His wife's surname is also illegible (□). He placed sixty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination; his Metropolitan Examination rank is recorded as 十□, with the final character illegible [?].

translation_en:
Liu Ji, registered in a civilian household in Zhaozhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a government student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zemin; he was second in birth order, aged forty, and born on the second day of an illegible month [?]. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Guicai, his father Neng, and his mother Lady □. Both parents were living. His elder brother’s name is illegible; his younger brothers were Hui, Jiang, and Lan. He married Guo □ [?]. He placed eighty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Xing, registered in a civilian household in Rong County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Zongcheng; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the tenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Tianzhang, an Instructor of Medicine; his grandfather was Qian, his father Congjing, his mother Lady Leng, and his stepmother Lady Hou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Fang and Gao, and he married Lady Zhao. He placed fifty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and three hundred forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Peng, registered in a military household in Yongming County, Daozhou, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Wanli; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Congren, his grandfather Zhaoxian, his father Kuan, and his mother Lady Tang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Qing and Ying, and he married Lady Ouyang. He placed forty-□ [?] in the Huguang Provincial Examination and two hundred twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yi Cheng, registered in an artisan household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, and originally from Wu County in the directly administered region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was □zai; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born in the eighth month on a day transcribed as □□三 [?]. His great-grandfather was Tong, with the annotation ‘all granted the title of Compiler in the Hanlin Academy’ [the persons included are unclear]; his grandfather was Jian, his father Pu, and his mother Lady Gu. A further Lady Chen appears after two illegible characters, leaving her relationship unclear [?]. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Fei, and he married Lady Jiang. He placed eighty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Ji: Registered in a military household in Hengshan County, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang [preceding character illegible]. His educational status is partly illegible [?]; his examination classic was the Classic of Poetry [?]. His courtesy name was Lizhi; he was third in birth order and aged thirty-seven [following character illegible]. His great-grandfather was Shuliang, his grandfather Weiqi, and his father Zhongfu. His mother was née Liu; the relationship of the following woman, née Wen, is obscured by illegible characters [?]. His mother was living and his father deceased. Wei (a tribute scholar) and Shen were apparently his elder brothers [?]; his younger brother was Xiu. He married a woman née Ouyang. He placed thirtieth or thirty-something [?] in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Gui: Registered in a military household in Fushan County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, he was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Tingyong; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the fourteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Zhixiao; his grandfather Yanbin was posthumously appointed Prefect; his father Yu was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; and his mother, née Fang, was invested with the title of Respectful Lady. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother Ke had formerly been Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; his younger brothers Zan and Yan were tribute scholars. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Wan: Registered in a civilian household in Quanzhou, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, he was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Zhonglian; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Minxiu, his grandfather Pu (a tribute scholar), his father Biao, and his mother née Jiang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yu, Yao, Lin, Huan, Sui, Lian, Jiu, Ying, and Qi. He married a woman née Liu. He placed fifth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Hong: Registered in an official household in Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, he was a student of the Imperial University specializing in an unidentified classic [title partly illegible]. His courtesy name was Zhongzhan; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the fifth day [preceding date characters illegible]. His great-grandfather Wenqing was posthumously appointed to a title beginning with “Right” [remainder illegible]; his grandfather Jie was posthumously appointed Right Censor-in-chief; and his father Xuan was Minister of Justice at Nanjing. His father's former wife is identified by two illegible characters; his mother, née Gu, was invested with the title of Lady. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jing (Secretary in the Secretariat of the Heir Apparent) and Lun (a student of the Imperial University); his younger brothers were Tong, Hui, Shen, Jin, and one whose name is illegible. He married a woman née Liu. He placed twenty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Cai 于材 was registered in a military household in Ningyuan County, Daozhou, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang; the next character is illegible [?]. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Guoyong, and he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-six, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Baoqing, his grandfather Zhigao, his father Menglian, and his mother née Li; his wife was née Ou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lin, Sen, and Bin, and his younger brothers Tang, Gui, and Ke; his concubine was née Liu. He placed nineteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Bi 趙璧 was registered in a military household of the Fujun Guard and was a native of Licheng County, Shandong. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Runfu, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Si, his grandfather Ba, his father Xing, and his mother née Jin. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Xi and Bao. His wife was née Wang; he subsequently married a woman née Hong. He placed seventy-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xun 王珣 was registered in a civilian household in Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Kewen, and he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hanying, his grandfather Yanliang, and his father Huaide; his father's former wife was née Xie, and his mother was née Fang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Ying and his younger brother Xuan; his wife was née Xie. He placed 123rd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yunzhong 劉允中 was registered in a military household in Gaoan County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhibao (執曓) [?], and he was third in birth order, aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qihong, his grandfather Gongfu, and his father Zhihai; his mother's surname is illegible. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shizhong and his younger brother Quanzhong; his wife's surname is illegible. His rank in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination is illegible (□□□); his Metropolitan Examination rank is partly illegible (四□□) [?].

Tian Duo, of civilian registration in Yangcheng County, Zezhou, Shanxi, was a student of an illegible category [?] specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zhenzhi; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on an illegible date [?]. His great-grandfather was Shizhao; his grandfather, Fu, was Left Administration Vice Commissioner; his father, Cong, was a Station Master; his mother's name is illegible [?]. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Kuang and his younger brother Fu; he married a woman of the Zhao family. He ranked twentieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 347th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Shao, of civilian registration in Chaoyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Tingshu; he was second in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fourteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Huai, his grandfather Congzhe, his father Yuanyi, and his mother a woman of the Jiang family. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Jing and his younger brothers Shou, Chou, and Shen; he married a woman of the Fang family. He ranked sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Demei, of civilian registration in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Kemei; he was fifth in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the thirtieth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Shihong, was a Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his grandfather was Tingming and his father Chengzhong. His mother was a woman of the Lin family, and his stepmothers were women of the Cai and Chen families. Both parents were living. He married a woman of the Zheng family. He ranked forty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zhen, of military registration in the □□ Front Guard [?], Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Daheng; he was first in birth order, aged forty-four, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was De, his grandfather Xian, and his father Shan. His mother was a woman of the Jiang family; one stepmother's name is illegible [?], and another was a woman of the Yu family. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Fu; he married a woman of the Cai family. His ranks in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and the Metropolitan Examination are illegible [?].

translation_en:
Shen Yuan 沈元 belonged to a medical household registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of an illegible category, specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Shanzhi, and ranked first among his brothers; he was forty-seven, and his birth date is illegible. His great-grandfather was Zongde, his grandfather Gongji, and his father Rumei; his mother's name is illegible. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Jian. He married Lady Chen and subsequently married a woman whose surname is illegible. He placed at an illegible rank in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Jian 高鑑 belonged to a military household registered in Xinyang Guard, Henan, and was a native of Taikang County. He was a student of the Directorate of Education, specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Keming, and ranked second among his brothers; his age is recorded as “two-eight,” apparently twenty-eight [?], and he was born on the second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Qiong, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was Lady Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Duo, and he married Lady Wu. He placed sixteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Chun 孫春 belonged to a military household registered in Weishi County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. He was a student of the Directorate of Education, specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Yiyuan, and ranked second among his brothers; he was thirty and was born on the fourth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was En, his grandfather Zhen, a Judge in a Salt Distribution Commission, and his father Ying; his mother was Lady Tian and his stepmother Lady Wang. He had living parents and grandparents. His elder brother Tai was a County Registrar, and his younger brother was Qi 桼. He married Lady Ren. He placed forty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and [illegible hundreds digit] hundred and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Jue 馮珏 belonged to a civilian household registered in Zhuji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. He was a county school student, specialized in the Book of Rites, had the courtesy name Liyu, and ranked tenth among his brothers; he was twenty-five and was born on the sixteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Boming, his grandfather Wei, and his father Qian, a District Magistrate; his mother's name is illegible. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ying and Guan, and his wife's name is illegible. His Zhejiang Provincial Examination ranking is illegible [?]; he placed seventy-[illegible final digit] in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Xuan, registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of an illegible category [?]; he specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Deyu, was third in birth order, and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fude, his grandfather Minwen, his father Zong, and his mother née Wang; both parents were living. His elder brother was Pu, his younger brothers Zhang and Zhuo, and his wife née Zhan. He placed thirty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Hao, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student; he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals, had the courtesy name Siqin, was fifth in birth order, and was aged forty-one, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Junli, his grandfather Yuanshan, his father Yong, and his mother née Zheng; both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Jiong and Mian, and his wife was née Yang. He placed sixty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo An, registered in Yiyang County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student; he specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Shitai, was tenth in birth order, and was aged forty-nine, born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dazhen, his grandfather Yunjing, his father Shimin, and his mother née Wang; both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Chongning, and his wife was née Guo. He placed eightieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng He, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to an artisan household and was a Confucian scholar; he specialized in the Book of Rites, had the courtesy name Tingyao, was third in birth order, and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wende, his grandfather Jin, his father Yu (granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice), and his mother née Chen (granted the title of Lady of Peace); both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhuo (Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice), his younger brothers Xuan and Yu, and his wife née Chen. He placed third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
□□ Jin [?], registered in a military household in Chaling County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of an illegible category [?] specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jixi; he ranked seventh in birth order, was aged thirty-five, and was born on an illegible day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ru, a Case Reviewer; his grandfather was Jie, a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father was Hu, also a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue. His father's principal wife was née Tan, granted the title Lady of Suitability; his birth mother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ao and Kai, both Honorary Officials; Tan, a National University student; Dian; Fu; and Wu. His younger brothers were Ao (鏖) and □□ [?]. He married a woman née Wu. He placed seventy-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Chao, registered in a military household in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Huayue; he ranked second in birth order, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ziyun, his grandfather was Shizhen, and his father was Lian, a National University student. His father's principal wife was née Chen, and his birth mother was née Zheng. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Miao, and his younger brother was Xun. He married a woman née Yu. He placed seventeenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 304th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Wenlin, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Runyu; he ranked ninth in birth order, was aged forty-one, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Yizheng, his grandfather was Tingguan, and his father was Mengyang. His father's principal wife was née Li, and his birth mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wenying and Wenxiang, the latter a National University student; his younger brothers were Wenzhang, Wencong, and Wenguang. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Lan, registered in a civilian household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Wenlan; he ranked third in birth order, was aged thirty-three, and was born on an illegible day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather was Tong, granted the title Supervising Secretary; and his father was Pin, a Right Administration Vice Commissioner. His mother was née Lu, granted the title Lady of Meekness. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Cheng, a provincial graduate (juren); his younger brothers were Tao, Shen, Pu, and Xun. He married a woman née Wang. He placed seventieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination; his Metropolitan Examination rank is recorded as 四□□ [?].

Dian De 點得 [?], registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, directly administered territory, belonged to a civilian household; two illegible characters precede the Book of Documents, apparently indicating his examination specialization [?]. His courtesy name was Tingmo. Second in birth order, he was aged forty-one and was born on the nineteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ruqing, his grandfather Min, and his father Bao; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Changping, and his younger brothers were Changmin and Changzu. He married a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Bo 孫博, registered in Jingzhou, Hejian Prefecture, directly administered territory, belonged to a civilian household and served as Assistant Instructor in the Jinan Prefectural School in Shandong. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuezhi. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingrang, his grandfather Shugong [?], and his father Sheng; his mother was née Du. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Kai, and his younger brothers were Heng and Chen. He married a woman née Liu. He placed fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jiugong 張九功, registered in Shanzhou, Henan Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xuzhi. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Minzhong, his grandfather’s name is illegible, and his father was Qing, a former District Magistrate. His mother was née Tian, and his stepmother was née Shen. His grandfather and parents were living. His elder brother was Jiugao, and his younger brothers were Jiuxu, Jiucheng, Jiurong, Jiujing, and Jiuqu. He married a woman née Sun. He placed sixteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Lu 熊祿, registered in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yuegui. Eighth in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Menggong, his grandfather Zefu, and his father Pengsheng; his mother was née Zhang. His grandfather and parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiang and Fu, and his younger brother was You. He married a woman née Wan. His Provincial Examination jurisdiction is illegible, and his rank is partly illegible, ending in seven [?]; he placed twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Weng Xin 翁信 was registered in a military household in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian [preceding character illegible]; his student status is partly illegible [?], and his examination classic was the Book of Odes [verb illegible]. His courtesy name was Yicheng. He was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on an illegible day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Duo, his grandfather Heng, and his father Lun; his mother was Lady Chen [following character illegible]. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Shuo, and he married Lady Li. He ranked fifty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 318th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Long Tengxiao 龍騰霄 was registered in a civilian household in Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shifu. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yanchen, his grandfather Mengduo, and his father Lin, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); his mother was Lady Li. His mother alone was living. He married Lady Li. He ranked twenty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Zong 郭宗 was registered in a military household in Liaohai Guard, Liaodong, and was a native of Poyang County, Jiangxi. His student status is partly illegible [?]; he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zonglu. He was second in birth order, aged twenty-two, and born on the twentieth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Cheng; his mother was Lady Shi. Both parents were living. His elder brother Hong was a student of the Directorate of Education. He married Lady Li and was subsequently betrothed to Lady Long. He ranked twenty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Che Xi 車璽 was registered in an artisan household in Wanping County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Zezhou, Shanxi. He was an added-quota student at the prefectural school and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Guozhi. He was second in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Duo, his grandfather Xuan, and his father Yu; his mother was Lady Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Bao; his younger brothers were Gong, Qi, Cong, Xuan, Lin, Qi, and Rong. His wife's name is illegible [?]. He ranked ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Song Li, registered in a civilian household in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, was originally from Qiantang County, Zhejiang. An additional-quota government student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Weiyin and was third in birth order, aged twenty-three, born on an illegible day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gong, his grandfather Yongshan, and his father Tingyu; his mother was née Lan and his stepmother née Wen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiang and Fu, and his younger brothers Yu, Qi, and You. He was betrothed to a woman née Lu. He ranked first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Ang was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Tianfeng and was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, born on the ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanji, his grandfather Zhongren, and his father Gong, an Honorary Official; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Wen, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Ding. His wife was née Liu. He ranked forty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zehe was registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Zhile and was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-eight, born on the twelfth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongbian, his grandfather Shucheng, and his father Rucai; his mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Kexie and Xixian. His wife was née Lin. He ranked fifty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sha Bi was registered in a military household in Shangcheng County, Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Tingyu and was second in birth order, aged thirty, born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chengfu, his grandfather Zhonghai, and his father Min; his mother was née Feng. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Shen. His Provincial Examination location and rank are illegible [?]; he ranked 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Jian 錢鑑 belonged to a military household registered in the Front Guard of an illegible place ending in “zhou” [?]; the following particulars are illegible, beginning with 國 [?]. He was forty-five years old, born on an illegible day within the first ten days of the first month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather’s name is illegible; his father was Zhen, formerly Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; and his mother, née Yu, held the conferred title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His younger brother’s name is illegible, and his wife was née Wang. He ranked eighty-[?] in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bao Ding 包鼎 belonged to a civilian household registered in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Rudiao and was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, born on the first day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Chengfu; his grandfather was Gui, who had been granted the privilege of wearing an official cap and girdle under provisions of imperial grace; his father was Jun; his mother was née Wang; and his stepmother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Nai, a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort, Zi, and Mi. His wife was née Shen. He ranked 26th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Ming 宋明 belonged to a military household registered in Xun County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Weiyuan and was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, born on the second day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Shuzhao; his grandfather was Chun; his father was Shu; his mother was née Zou; and his stepmother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Liang. His wife was née Lu, and his subsequent wife was née Liu. He ranked 95th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Cong 宋琮 belonged to a civilian household registered in Longxi County, Gongchang Prefecture, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had an illegible courtesy name and was third in birth order, aged forty-three, born on the sixteenth day of the intercalary sixth month. His great-grandfather was Wenyi; his grandfather was Jingrong; his father was Youliang; and his mother was née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. The name or names of his elder brother or brothers are illegible [?]. His wife was née Zhu. His rank in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination is illegible; he ranked 97th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sixth in birth order and aged twenty-nine, he was born on an illegible day of the intercalary second month. His great-grandfather was Chang□, his father Gongjie, and his mother née Huang. His mother alone was surviving. His elder brothers were Tao and Jun. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Zhu. He placed twenty-□ in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shao, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jiucheng. Fourth in birth order and aged twenty-three, he was born on the twenty-second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yuncai; his grandfather, Yu, had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under provisions for imperial favor. His father was Sheng and his mother née Zhang; both parents were living. His elder brother was Ying, and his younger brother’s name is transcribed as 𥠧 [?]. He married a woman née Chen. He placed seventieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and apparently 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination (the text reads “一二三” [?]).

Zong Yue, registered in a civilian household in Yixing County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tingwei. Fourth in birth order and aged twenty-eight, he was born on the first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongke, his grandfather Youyuan, and his father Lin. His father’s former wife was née Zhou, and his mother was née Cui. His father alone was surviving. His elder brothers were Qin, Xiao (a Steward, dianshan), and Yi; his younger brother was Yue. He married a woman née Pan. He placed ninety-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xiang, registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Imperial University; his classical specialization and courtesy name are illegible. Second in birth order and aged twenty-eight, he was born on the sixth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Xiaolian, his grandfather’s name is illegible, and his father was Hua. His mother was née Li, and his stepmother née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were □ and Yu. He married a woman née Feng. His rank in the Guangdong Provincial Examination is illegible; he placed 190-□ in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Bangrui 陳邦瑞 was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture; the preceding four characters and his educational status are illegible. His classical specialization is illegible, and his courtesy name appears to be Mengrui [?]. He was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on an illegible day within the first ten days of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengyue, his grandfather Congji, his father Kesi, and his mother Lady Yu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Bangying, Bangshao, and Bangxin, and he married Lady Zheng. He ranked eighty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Tingyong 馬廷用 was registered in a civilian household in Xichong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Liangzuo. He was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the thirtieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuyin, his grandfather Juezhao, his father Duo (a student of the Imperial University), and his mother Lady Jia. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Tinghui; his younger brothers were Tingshu, Tingxiang, and Tingjun. He married Lady He. He ranked forty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Rong 林榮 was registered in a military household in Hepu County, Lianzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhongren. He was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sancai, his grandfather Zhong, and his father Zhenji; his father's former wife was Lady Fan, and his mother was Lady Ou. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Guang, Qing 慶, and Qing 清; his younger brother was Hui. He married Lady Ren. He ranked forty-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Ti, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shunjing. Second in birth order, he was aged 31 and born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongyong, an official of a River Fisheries Office; his grandfather was Shangbai; his father was Tiguang; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother Kai was a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue. His wife was née Lin. He placed 56th in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 52nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Lin, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Wenyu. Second in birth order, he was aged 43 and born on the eighth day of the intercalary sixth month. His great-grandfather was Shichang; his grandfather was Mao; his father was Xin; and his mother was née Xia. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xuan. His first wife was née Ji, and his subsequent wife was née Xu. He placed 108th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Zefang, registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county Confucian school. His classical specialization is illegible (□□); his courtesy name was Zhengfu. Sixth in birth order, he was aged 32 and born on the fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zong□; his grandfather was Wei□; and his father was Ming. His father's former wife was née Chen; his stepmother was Chen□ [?]; and his birth mother was née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers are recorded as Ze□□ming [?; the division between names is unclear], with the title Professor annotated here, followed by Zehe, Zewen, and Zeren; his younger brother was Zeyu. His wife was née Chen. He placed 85th in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 71st in the Metropolitan Examination.

An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Maocheng, ranked third among his brothers, was thirty-seven, and was born on the twenty-first day of the seventh lunar month. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Tinghui, ranked second among his brothers, was twenty-five, and was born on the third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Yu (Vice Director of Sacrifices), his father Jing, and his mother née Li. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Chen and his younger brother Lian. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed 67th in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Wen and his father Yan; his father’s former wife was née Sun, and his mother was née Liang. Both his parents were deceased. An illegible relationship designation precedes the names Yi, Heng, Liang, and Guang [?]. He married a woman whose surname is illegible. Six characters preceding his Metropolitan Examination rank are illegible; he placed 88th in that examination.

王本儉〔貫湖廣黃州府麻城縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字節之，行二，年四十、八月初十日生〕。曾祖舜舉，祖友誠，父孟良，母王氏，繼母徐氏。嚴侍下，兄邦，弟郭、邵、邰、鄲，娶鄭氏。湖廣鄉試第九名，會試第二百四十六名。

王建〔貫江西南昌府進賢縣軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字成中，行二，年四十三，五月初二日生〕。曾祖天麒，祖仕恭，父子謨，母張氏。永感下，兄□，娶萬氏，繼娶黃氏、手氏。□□□□□□名，會試第一百七□名。
translation_en:
Ding Ji, registered in a civilian household in Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; his Imperial University status is partly illegible [?]. He specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Yufu, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged twenty-two, born on the tenth [?] day of the fifth month (the character after “ten” is illegible). His great-grandfather was Hui; his grandfather, Ning, was a Guard Registrar; his father was Yuanji, and his mother was née Qian. Both parents were living. He was betrothed to a woman née Zhang. He placed thirteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jing Mao was registered in a military household in Ningyuan Guard, Huguang, and was a native of Linfen County, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Tingchun, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-two, born on the twelfth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather, Deguang; his father, Yuan; and his mother, née Zhai. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Fang, Chang 菖, and Chang 萇. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed eighty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Benjian was registered in a civilian household in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Jiezhi, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged forty, born on the tenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Shunju; his grandfather, Youcheng; his father, Mengliang; his mother, née Wang; and his stepmother, née Xu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Bang, and his younger brothers were Guo, Shao, Tai, and Dan. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jian was registered in a military household in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Chengzhong, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged forty-three, born on the second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Tianqi; his grandfather, Shigong; his father, Zimo; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother’s name is illegible. He married a woman née Wan and subsequently women née Huang and née Shou [?]. The examination designation and placing preceding his Metropolitan Examination result are illegible; he placed 170-something [?] in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳湜〔貫直隸徽州府歙縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字一清，行一，年四十二，二月二十九日生〕。曾祖天保，祖泰童，父惠祖，母凌氏。具慶下，弟溥、瀅、汶，娶曹氏。應天府鄉試第七十一名，會試第二百十一名。

汪舜民〔貫直隸徽州府婺源縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治春秋，字從仁，行一，年二十六，九月二十九日生〕。曾祖彪，祖桐，父魁，母游氏。重慶下，弟天民、希民、生民、濟民，娶江氏。應天府鄉試第八十七名，會試第二百六十八名。
translation_en:
Wenren Zu 聞人珇, courtesy name Defu, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the sixteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Qian; his grandfather, Yuan; and his father, Mo, an Investigating Censor. His father's former wife was née Zheng, and his mother was née Shao. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brother, Gui, was a Station Master; his younger brother was Gong. His wife was née Wang. He placed eleventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Zhong 黃鍾, courtesy name Bolu, was registered in a civilian household in Hezhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the fifteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Rongshan; his grandfather, Zitong, an Astrologer; and his father, Hu. His father's former wife was née Su, and his mother was née Wang. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Wanli, an Astrologer, and Wanquan. He placed thirtieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shi 吳湜, courtesy name Yiqing, was registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was forty-two years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Tianbao; his grandfather, Taitong; his father, Huizu; and his mother, née Ling. Both his parents were living. His younger brothers were Pu, Ying, and Wen, and his wife was née Cao. He placed seventy-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shunmin 汪舜民, courtesy name Congren, was registered in a civilian household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-six years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Biao; his grandfather, Tong; his father, Kui; and his mother, née You. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Tianmin, Ximin, Shengmin, and Jimin, and his wife was née Jiang. He placed eighty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉翔〔貫直隸河間府獻縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字九霄，行三，年四十，十月初三日生〕。曾祖彥中，祖希賢，父瑄〔府經歷〕，母韓氏。永感下，兄聊、翱〔貢士〕，娶蕭氏，繼娶蘇氏。順天府鄉試第七十六名，會試第二百十名。

劉琬〔貫江西袁州府宜春縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字德資，行二，年三十四，七月十六日生〕。曾祖以文，祖爾亨，父信忠〔縣丞〕，母胡氏。具慶下，兄球〔貢士〕，弟璨，娶歐氏。□西鄉試第八十四名，會試第一百二十五名。
translation_en:
Shen Qing, registered in Gui’an County, Zhejiang, and a native of Funing Guard in Zhili, specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Lianfu, he was first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zongben, his grandfather Chengqi, his father Wenli, and his mother née Zhu; his mother alone was still living, his wife was née Xu, and he placed twenty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Rong, of military household registration in Liling County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yongshi, he was second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twentieth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yusheng, his grandfather Wenxiang, his father Zhizhong, and his mother née Sima; his father alone was still living, his elder brother was Fu, his younger brothers were Qi and Li, his wife was née Tang, and he placed seventy-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xiang, of civilian household registration in Xian County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jiuxiao, he was third among his brothers, and he was aged forty, born on the third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yanzhong, his grandfather Xixian, his father Xuan (a prefectural registrar), and his mother née Han; both parents were deceased, his elder brothers were Liao and Ao (a tribute scholar, gongshi), he married a woman née Xiao and subsequently a woman née Su, and he placed seventy-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Wan, of civilian household registration in Yichun County, Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Dezi, he was second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yiwen, his grandfather Erheng, his father Xinzhong (a county vice magistrate), and his mother née Hu; both parents were living, his elder brother was Qiu (a tribute scholar, gongshi), his younger brother was Can, his wife was née Ou, and he placed eighty-fourth in the Provincial Examination of □xi [Jiangxi?] and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Gai was registered in a civilian household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name □□ (illegible), was first in birth order, and was aged thirty-six, born on the seventeenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather’s name is illegible (□); his father was Pu, a Professor; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Bo, Guo, and Tang, and his wife was née Bian. He placed one hundredth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ouyang Fu was registered in a military household of Hengzhou Guard, Huguang, and was a native of Anren County, Hengzhou Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Mengheng, was first in birth order, and was aged forty-one, born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shengxian; his grandfather was Wei’an; his father was Shigao; and his mother was née Tan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xi, He, Rong, and Shu, the last a government school student, and his wife was née Chen. He placed thirty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and two hundred fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Long was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Shiyong, was first in birth order, and was aged forty, born on the third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Haocun; his grandfather was Hongzheng; his father was Jichuan; and his mother was née Yao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Feng, Hui, and Yan, and his wife was née Tan. He placed fourteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pu Gang was registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Nanjin, was first in birth order, and was aged forty, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziwen, an Official of Philanthropy; his grandfather was Wanpu; his father was Yongjian; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Lian and E, and his wife was née Huang. He placed fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Hong, courtesy name Zhongguang, was registered in a military household under the Office of the Disciplinary Officer of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Rizhao County, Shandong. He was a supernumerary member of a military household and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-two and born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liugong, his grandfather Fu, and his father Gui; his mother was née Song. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yu, and his younger brothers were Shi and Ning. He married a woman née Yan, subsequently married a woman née Wu, and was betrothed to a woman née Jiang. He ranked forty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chang Heng, courtesy name Wentong, was registered in a military household in Hejin County, Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. He was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Classic of Documents. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yancheng, his grandfather Shiying, and his father Jingxian; his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Mao, and he married a woman née Wu. He ranked sixteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Ding, courtesy name Liangjin, was registered in a civilian household in Anyang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan. He was a prefectural school student and specialized in the Classic of Documents. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty and born on the twenty-second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhi, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Chen; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhao, and his younger brothers were Jian, Luan, and Yu. He married a woman née Ma. He ranked sixtieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zihua, courtesy name Zishi, was registered in a military household of the Dali Guard, Yunnan, and was a native of Juzhou, Shandong. He was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. Second in birth order, he was aged forty and born on the thirteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Yuan, and his father Chun; his mother was née Chen. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Rong, and his younger brother Mao. He married a woman née Cheng and subsequently married a woman née Wu. He ranked second in the Provincial Examination of [place illegible: □□] and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.
