鄒賢〔貫四川成都府內江縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字世用，行二，生五月初八日生〕。曾祖明道，祖世清，父琳，母羅氏。嚴侍下，兄永德，弟永哲，娶門氏，繼聘李氏。四川鄉試第五十七名，會試第三十九名。

丁積〔貫江西贛州府寧都縣匠籍，縣學生，治詩經，字彥誠，行一，年三十二，十二月初十日生〕。曾祖德紹，祖伯高，父時學，母劉氏。永感下，娶羅氏。江西鄉試第九十二名，會試第一百三十六名。

丁昶〔貫雲南蒙化衛軍籍，湖廣襄陽縣人，國子生，治書經，字德輝，行六，年三十六，十二月初九日生〕。曾祖謙，祖克讓，父誠，前母唐氏，母莊氏。慈侍下，兄昱、曆、暠、昭、杲，弟暲，娶江氏，繼娶楊氏。雲南鄉試第十三名，會試第一百八十五名。

周仲芳〔貫湖廣武昌府江夏縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字繼遠，行一，年四十九，十月十二日生〕。曾祖餘慶，祖成，父旭，母王氏。具慶下，弟仲良、仲奇、仲英，娶程氏。湖廣鄉試第七十六名，會試第一百五名。
translation_en:
Zou Xian 鄒賢, courtesy name Shiyong, was registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan; he was a student of the Directorate of Education, specialized in the Book of Documents, and ranked second among his brothers; he was born on the eighth day of the fifth lunar month (the preceding 生 is anomalous [?], and no age is given). His great-grandfather was Mingdao, his grandfather Shiqing, his father Lin, and his mother Lady Luo; his father was living and his mother deceased, his elder brother was Yongde, his younger brother Yongzhe, and he married Lady Men and subsequently became betrothed to Lady Li; he placed fifty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Ji 丁積, courtesy name Yancheng, was registered in an artisan household in Ningdu County, Ganzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi; he was a county government school student, specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-two years old, and was born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deshao, his grandfather Bogao, his father Shixue, and his mother Lady Liu; both parents were deceased, and he married Lady Luo; he placed ninety-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Chang 丁昶, courtesy name Dehui, was registered in a military household of Menghua Guard, Yunnan, and was originally from Xiangyang County, Huguang; he was a student of the Directorate of Education, specialized in the Book of Documents, ranked sixth among his brothers, was thirty-six years old, and was born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian, his grandfather Kerang, his father Cheng, his father's former wife Lady Tang, and his mother Lady Zhuang; his mother was living and his father deceased, his elder brothers were Yu, Li, Gao, Zhao, and Gao (昱、曆、暠、昭、杲), his younger brother was Zhang, and he married Lady Jiang and subsequently Lady Yang; he placed thirteenth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Zhongfang 周仲芳, courtesy name Jiyuan, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangxia County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang; he was a student of the Directorate of Education, specialized in the Book of Documents, ranked first among his brothers, was forty-nine years old, and was born on the twelfth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuqing, his grandfather Cheng, his father Xu, and his mother Lady Wang; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Zhongliang, Zhongqi, and Zhongying, and he married Lady Cheng; he placed seventy-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

金清〔貫浙江紹興府會稽縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字宗源，行二，年三十三，正月二十六日生〕。曾祖道宗，祖文貴，父進，母沈氏。具慶下，兄宗，弟浩，娶馮氏。浙江鄉試第三十四名，會試第三百七名。

朱昂〔貫湖廣辰州府沅陵縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字廷舉，行二，年四十一，八月初八日生〕。曾祖秉彝，祖成山，父諒，母向氏。慈侍下，兄昱，弟景，娶王氏。湖廣鄉試第三十名，會試第三百十四名。

陳寛〔貫直隸真定府冀州新河縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字裕夫，行三，年四十一，五月十二日生〕。曾祖茂大，祖元莊，父誠，母周氏。永感下，兄安、宏，娶王氏。順天府鄉試第一百二十六名，會試第一百十五名。

鍾雅〔貫廣東惠州府歸善縣，民籍，府學生，治春秋，字大章，行一，年三十，十二月二十一日生〕。曾祖景陽，祖鐸，父元，母王氏。具慶下，弟耀，娶王氏。廣東鄉試第四十五名，會試第一百三十二名。
translation_en:
Jin Qing 金清, registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zongyuan, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daozong, his grandfather Wengui, his father Jin, and his mother née Shen; both parents were living; his elder brother was Zong and his younger brother Hao; his wife was née Feng; he placed thirty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 307th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Ang 朱昂, registered in a military household in Yuanling County, Chenzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Tingju, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged forty-one, born on the eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bingyi, his grandfather Chengshan, his father Liang, and his mother née Xiang; his mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brother was Yu and his younger brother Jing; his wife was née Wang; he placed thirtieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 314th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Kuan 陳寛, registered in a civilian household in Xinhe County, Jizhou Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yufu, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged forty-one, born on the twelfth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Maoda, his grandfather Yuanzhuang, his father Cheng, and his mother née Zhou; both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were An and Hong; his wife was née Wang; he placed 126th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Ya 鍾雅, registered in a civilian household in Guishan County, Huizhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Dazhang, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingyang, his grandfather Duo, his father Yuan, and his mother née Wang; both parents were living; his younger brother was Yao; his wife was née Wang; he placed forty-fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

紀傑〔貫順天府東安縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字季仁，行四，年二十四，四月二十八日生〕。曾祖繼本〔翰林院檢討〕，祖東〔行人司司正、太僕寺少卿〕，父侃〔右僉都御史〕，母張氏〔封淑人〕。嚴侍下，兄德容、德章〔貢士〕、德恢〔太僕寺寺丞〕，娶董氏。順天府鄉試第十名，會試第四十四名。

陳綺〔貫浙江台州府太平縣竈籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字于章，行十，年三十，二月二十三日生〕。曾祖思，祖伯初，父允謙，母顧氏。永感下，兄緒、繩、經、紘、維、綸，弟紀，娶季氏，繼娶林氏。浙江鄉試第二十名，會試第一百二十四名。

鄭玨〔貫河南開封府歸德州民籍，州學生，治書經，字廷貴，行一，年三十，十一月初八日生〕。曾祖中，祖真，父宣，母鮑氏。具慶下，弟琇，娶張氏。河南鄉試第十五名，會試第一百九十九名。

周南〔貫浙江處州府縉雲縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字文化，行二，年三十一，八月初九日生〕。曾祖伯玉，祖溫善，父瓘〔訓導〕，母張氏。具慶下，兄魯，弟邦、男，娶虞氏。浙江鄉試第八十八名，會試第三百三十五名。
translation_en:
Ji Jie 紀傑, courtesy name Jiren, was registered in a civilian household in Dong’an County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; fourth in birth order, he was aged twenty-four and born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Jiben, an Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy; his grandfather was Dong, Chief Messenger in the Office of Transmission and Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud; his father was Kan, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief; and his mother, née Zhang, was granted the title of Lady (shuren). His father was living and his mother deceased; his elder brothers were Derong, Dezhang, a tribute scholar, and Dehui, Assistant Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud; his wife was née Dong. He placed tenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Qi 陳綺, courtesy name Yuzhang, was registered in a salt-producing household in Taiping County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Documents; tenth in birth order, he was aged thirty and born on the twenty-third day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Si, his grandfather Bochu, his father Yunqian, and his mother née Gu. Both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Xu, Sheng, Jing, Hong, Wei, and Lun, and his younger brother was Ji; he married a woman née Ji and subsequently a woman née Lin. He placed twentieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Jue 鄭玨, courtesy name Tinggui, was registered in a civilian household in Guide Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, and was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Classic of Documents; first in birth order, he was aged thirty and born on the eighth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Zhen, his father Xuan, and his mother née Bao. Both parents were living; his younger brother was Xiu, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed fifteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 199th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Nan 周南, courtesy name Wenhua, was registered in a military household in Jinyun County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes; second in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and born on the ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Boyu, his grandfather Wenshan, his father Guan, an Assistant Instructor, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living; his elder brother was Lu, and his younger brothers were Bang and Nan; his wife was née Yu. He placed eighty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 335th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
□ Zheng (□政), courtesy name Yide, was registered in a civilian household in Ye County, Yuzhou, Nanyang Prefecture, [He]nan [?]. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Jinzhao; his grandfather, Long; his father, Ying; and his mother, née Han. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Mao, Fang, and Jun, and he married a woman née Peng. He placed sixty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 310th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guan Tong (管通), courtesy name Yanheng, was registered in a civilian household in Dongguang County, Jingzhou, Hejian Prefecture, in the metropolitan region (Zhili). A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he was first in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the twelfth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Youcai; his father, Sheng, a Chief Clerk; and his mother, née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Da, Dao, Xun, Zun, Di, Sui, and Kui, and he married a woman née Ren. He placed seventy-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Yong (錢鏞), courtesy name Yongsheng, was registered in a civilian household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Hua; his grandfather, Gui; his father, Jing; and his mother, née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tang and his younger brother, Jian. He was betrothed to a woman née Li. He placed tenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 339th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Hong (姜洪), courtesy name Xifan, was registered in a civilian household in Guangde Subprefecture, in the metropolitan region (Zhili). A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Chongming, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather, Chuqian; his father, Yun; and his mother, née Yu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yuan and his younger brother, Pu, a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Yao. His Provincial Examination entry is damaged: it begins with Ying and preserves a rank ending in twenty-seven [?]. He placed 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

馮瑢〔貫直隸徽州府績溪縣，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字時鳴，行二，年四十四，九月十□日生〕。曾祖敏政，祖子攸，父義觀〔義官〕，母陳氏。慈侍下，兄璇，弟珹、瓏、玥、理、玩、璉，娶程氏。應□鄉試第三十五名，會試第一百三十二名。
translation_en:
Jin Heng 金珩, courtesy name Wenming, was a student of the Imperial University from Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, registered in a civilian household. He specialized in the Book of Rites, was second in birth order, and was aged twenty-seven, born on the thirtieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhengyan, a County Magistrate; his grandfather was Shou, a Department Magistrate; and his father was Zhou. His mother was née Chen and his stepmother née Zhao; both parents were living. His elder brother was Huan, and his younger brothers were Lu and Lian. He married a woman née Ge. He ranked seventy-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo He 過鶴, courtesy name Jiugao, was a student of the Imperial University from Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, registered in a military household. He specialized in the Book of Odes, was third in birth order, and was aged thirty, born on the sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongyuan, his grandfather Demin, and his father Lang; his mother was née Huang. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Feng and Peng. He married a woman née Huang. He ranked forty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Hong 孫紘, courtesy name Wenmian, was a student of the Imperial University from Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, registered in a civilian household. He specialized in the Book of Changes, was first in birth order, and was aged thirty-five, born on the ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuzu, an Instructor; his grandfather was Hengsheng, and his father Shangying; his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked fifty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Rong 馮瑢, courtesy name Shiming, was a student of the Imperial University from Jixi County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, registered in a civilian household. He specialized in the Book of Rites, was second in birth order, and was aged forty-four, born on the tenth [?] day of the ninth lunar month (the day is transcribed as 十□). His great-grandfather was Minzheng, his grandfather Ziyou, and his father Yiguan, who held the honorary title of Official for Philanthropy. His mother was née Chen; his mother alone was living. His elder brother was Xuan, and his younger brothers were Cheng, Long, Yue, Li, Wan, and Lian. He married a woman née Cheng. He ranked thirty-fifth in the Ying□ [?] Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
□ Xuan (surname illegible), courtesy name Wenyong, was registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was seventh in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather was Zhou, honorarily conferred the title of Investigating Censor; and his father was Shufu. His father's principal wife was née Lü, and his birth mother was née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Xuan (烜), and his younger brothers were Xi and Can. He married a woman née Ye. He ranked sixty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lian Sheng, courtesy name Wenchang, was registered in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twelfth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youwen, his grandfather Wang, and his father Qi. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Xiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Rong and Gui, and his younger brother was Mao. He married a woman née Li. He ranked 101st in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Lun, courtesy name Tianxu, was registered in Pingliang Guard, Shaanxi, in a military household, and was a native of Yancheng County, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the thirteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Gui, and his father Jing. His mother was née Fan, and his stepmother was née Jin. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Jie, and his younger brothers were Zuo and You. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née He. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Wenyu, courtesy name Dehui, was registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A county-school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Jingwen, and his father Ju. His father's former wife was née Zheng, and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Wenqi. He married a woman née Lin. He ranked seventy-seventh in the Provincial Examination of □□ [place illegible] and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Yizhen, registered in a civilian household in Changshan County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was an additional student at the county school and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Benliang; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sijing, posthumously granted the title of District Magistrate; his grandfather was Lin, an Assistant Prefect; his father was Zan, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Liu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Weizhen and Youzhen, and his wife was née Xu. He placed sixtieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Hong, registered in a military household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Borong; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the eighteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Miaogui, his grandfather Yao, his father Li, and his mother née Pu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Hongyi and Hongdao; his younger brothers were Hongzhi, Hongxing, and Hongde. His wife was née Yang. He placed fifteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Ti, registered in a civilian household in He Subprefecture, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was an additional student at the subprefectural school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shunqing; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chaoju, his grandfather Zhongren, his father Ying, and his mother née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Xiao and his younger brother Mu. He was betrothed to a woman née Guo. He placed sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhuo, registered in a military household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yongjian; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Lin, his father Lu, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qiao, a District Magistrate, and Chou. His wife was née Chen, and he subsequently married another woman née Chen. He placed sixty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
□ Qiu, whose surname is illegible, was registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household, and was a military student at the Pinghai Guard school. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yufu; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the eleventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanheng, his grandfather Chaojing, his father Biaoxiang, and his mother Lady Li. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yuru, and he married Lady Zhu. He placed sixty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Da was registered in Dahe Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household, and was a native of Chongming County. He was a student at the Huai’an Prefectural School and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Cundao; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged forty-one, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xingshi, his grandfather Zizhong, his father Wenxue, and his mother Lady Gu. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His younger brothers were Jin and Xun. He married Lady Zhu and subsequently married Lady Li and Lady Ding. He placed 118th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ji was registered in Fengxiang County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a military household. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shuzhi; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Lin, and his father Hao, a Supervisor (jianshi) [?]. His father’s former wife was Lady Sun, and his mother was Lady Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jin and Shen. He married Lady Tian and subsequently married Lady Jiao. He placed seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Fu was registered in Jixi County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yongnian; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Deyu, an Instructor; his grandfather was Shiliang, his father Daohong, and his mother Lady Fang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Ruqi and Ru□, the latter name partly illegible. He married Lady Zheng. He placed fifty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Shangyi, his grandfather Min 〔posthumously granted the title of Subprefect〕, his father Qing, and his mother née He. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Mao. He married a woman née Zheng and subsequently a woman née Wu. He placed sixty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Weng Jiefu was registered in a salt-producing household in □□ County, Fujian, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name is illegible [?]; he was forty-one years old, born on the seventeenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zongmeng, his grandfather Tinggui, his father Yuzhi, and his mother née Fang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Gong and Xun; his younger brothers were Dong, Liang, Mei, and Lang [?]. His wife was née Zheng. He ranked third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Gang was registered in a civilian household in Suining County, Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Tingxian; he was third in birth order, thirty-three years old, and born on the twelfth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Wengui, his father Yuansheng, and his mother née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Hu and Chang. His wife was née Wang. He ranked thirty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Ying was registered in a military household of the Shenwu Right Guard, was a native of Jiangdu County in Zhili, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Tingguang; he was first in birth order, thirty-one years old, and born on the nineteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Wang, his father Yan, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Cong and Qi. His wife was née Chao. He ranked 107th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Yi was registered in an official household of the Dingliao Right Guard in Liaodong, was a native of Huanggang County, Huguang, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shiyi; he was second in birth order, thirty-five years old, and born on the ninth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, a company commander; his grandfather was Liang, followed by two illegible characters [?]. His father's former wife was née Zhao, and his mother was also née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Li. His wife was née Wang. He ranked seventy-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; four characters giving further personal particulars are illegible. He was forty-one years old, born on the sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rongyi; his grandfather, Rong; his father, Jian; and his mother, née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Qing and Yuan, and his younger brothers Gao, Guang, and Xue. He married a woman née Fei. He placed fifty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ji was registered in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, in a civilian household. He was an additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Shiheng, and he was third in birth order, aged twenty-eight, born on the fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, posthumously granted the title of Minister; his grandfather was Zhongfu, Minister of Revenue and Adviser to the Heir Apparent; and his father was Lian, chief minister of the Eastern Court of Imperial Stud [?; the transcribed title is doubtful]. His father’s former wife, née Fang, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Virtue; his mother, née Zhang, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability; and his stepmother, née Jiang, was likewise granted the title of Lady of Suitability. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Lin, a magistrate, and Bin; his younger brothers were Xiang, Huan, Kai, and Mu. He married a woman née Lin. He placed forty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 334th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ping was registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, in a military household. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Weisheng, and he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanhui; his grandfather was Lin, granted the title of Assistant in a court; and his father was You, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. His mother, née Lu, was granted the title of Lady of Peace, and his stepmother was née Ni. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Gan and Yi. He married a woman née Xiao. He placed ninety-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ze was registered in Zezhou, Shanxi, in a civilian household. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Kemin, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, born on an illegible day within the first ten days of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shili; his grandfather, Wenshun; his father, Xiang, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother, née Qin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hao and Chun. He married a woman née Wang. He placed thirteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shao Liang, courtesy name Xinfu, was registered in a military household of the Tengxiang Left Guard and came from Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. An additional student at the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the tenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, his grandfather Furong, his father Zhong, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yi, and he was betrothed to a woman née Wang. He placed third in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Qingxiang, courtesy name Dezheng, was registered in a civilian household in Yudu County, Ganzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuchang, his grandfather Fangzhi, his father Duan, a Professor, and his mother née Sun. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Qingkui, Qingyun, Qingqi, Qinglin, and Qingyang. His wife was née Liu. He placed ninety-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Mian, courtesy name Fuzhou, was registered in a civilian household in Changyuan County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Heng, his father Cong, a Professor, his mother née Huang, and his stepmother née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Min; his younger brothers were Bao, Bian, Bing, Tan, Gao, 𣈥 [reading uncertain], and Qin. His wife was née Ren. He placed forty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Jin, courtesy name Tingshen, was registered in a military household in Wenxi County, Jiezhou Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the nineteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shu, his grandfather Dingyu, his father Bin, and his mother née Ren. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chun, Lun, and Hui. His wife was née Zhang; his subsequent wives were née Meng and née Wang. He placed twelfth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

□□mei [?], courtesy name Yuanyong, was registered in a military household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-seven [?], and born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuang, his grandfather Yong, and his father Cheng; his mother was née Zhao and his stepmother née Zou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tingchun and Tingbo, and his younger brothers Tingzhang, Tingzhe, and Tingpu. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently married [?] a woman née Xu. He ranked third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Guan, courtesy name Liangyu, was registered in a civilian household in Yongfeng County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Canran, his grandfather Shuliang, and his father Xi, an Instructor; his mother was née Liu and his stepmother née Dong. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Zao, and his younger brothers Xi, Yu, and Zhuan. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked thirty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 270th [?] in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Xuan, courtesy name Huaiyu, was registered in a civilian household in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student [?] specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the twelfth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Congyi, his grandfather Youzhi, and his father Fang; his mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Cong, and his younger brothers Jin and Ying. He married a woman née Jiao. He ranked eightieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ying, courtesy name Yuqing, was registered in a military household of the Suzhou Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a native of Xin’gan County, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the fifth day [?] of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Diji, his grandfather Qianhai, and his father Zongzheng; his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Gang and Ji. He married a woman née Li. He ranked thirty-sixth in the Ying□ [Yingtian?] Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Bin 劉彬, courtesy name Subin, was registered in a civilian household in Yong□□ [?], Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in birth order and was aged forty-two, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Haoqian; his grandfather, Rizhang; and his father, Dongxu. His father’s former wife and his mother were both née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yao, Huan, Yu, and Er. His wife was née Que. He placed seventy-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jing 李經, courtesy name Shichang, was registered in an officer household under the Wanquan Regional Military Commission and was a native of Linhuai County in the directly administered region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked sixth in birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the eleventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather Ji was a Battalion Commander, posthumously granted the title of Assistant Commander; his grandfather Yong and father Hui were Assistant Regional Military Commissioners. His mother, née Dong, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Virtue. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shou, acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, Jin, Shen, Zhen, and Chun; his younger brother was Shan. He married a woman née Yue and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed forty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jing 王鯨, courtesy name Dazhou, was registered in a military household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked third in birth order and was aged twenty-six, born on the twelfth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Congshan; his grandfather, Qian; and his father, Ji, an Imperial Son-in-Law. His father’s former wife was née Qu, Commandery Princess Jia□ [?]; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kun and Li; his younger brothers were Geng and Lin. His wife was née Xue. He placed thirty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 313th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Sheng 涂昇, courtesy name Qingyi, was registered in an artisan household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fifth in birth order and was aged twenty-eight, born on an illegible day within the first ten days of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Guosheng; his grandfather, Yongzai, received an illegible honorary title; and his father, Guan, was a Prefect. His mother, whose surname is illegible, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Peace; his stepmother, née Zhu, was granted the same title. He had living parents and grandparents. His elder brother was Bian; his younger brothers were Dan, □ [name illegible], and Hao. His wife was née Wu. He placed twelfth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Tai 張泰, courtesy name Shiheng, was registered in a civilian household in Suning County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An additional student of the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Odes; he ranked second in birth order and was twenty-seven sui, born on the ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Jingzu, and his father Wenxi; his mother was née Ma. Both parents were living. His wife was née Li. He placed sixtieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yan 李儼, courtesy name Zhongwei, was registered in a civilian household in Gaoyang County, Anzhou Subprefecture, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes; he ranked fourth in birth order and was forty-one sui, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deming, his grandfather Jin, and his father Furong; his mother was née Yan and his stepmother née Liang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xing, Xin, and Yuan; his wife was née Guo. He placed 105th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Yu 曹玉, courtesy name Derun, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents; he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-nine sui, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengzhuang, his grandfather Yi, and his father Zhong, a prefect; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Qi; his wife was née Zhu. He placed forty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Shirun 林時潤, courtesy name Dewen, was registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Odes; he ranked sixth in birth order and was forty-nine sui, born on the seventeenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youtie, his grandfather Fuyuan, and his father Mengming; his mother was née Zhan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Shiji; his wife was née Zhang. He placed fourteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Lian, courtesy name Qizhi, was registered in a military household of Pengcheng Guard and was a native of □□□ County [name illegible]. A military dependent, he specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked second in family order, and was aged thirty, born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Jie, his father Ning, and his mother née Li; both parents were living. His elder brother was Xun, and his younger brothers were Xuan 瑄 and Xuan 玹. He married a woman née Song and subsequently a woman née He. He placed ninety-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Huan, courtesy name Dechong, was registered in an officer household under the Shanxi Regional Military Commission. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked sixth in family order, and was aged thirty-six, born on the sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin, posthumously granted the title of Regional Military Commissioner; his grandfather was Ming, Regional Military Commissioner; and his father was Xin. His father's former wife was née Xiao, and his mother was née Sun; his mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xian, Yi, Fu, and You. He married a woman née Li. He placed second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Chong, courtesy name Dechong, was registered in a civilian household in Huai'an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked fifth in family order, and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Ling, his father Qian, and his mother née Lin; both parents were living. He married a woman née Wang. He placed eighteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yue, courtesy name Yangzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Anren County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked fifty-fifth in family order, and was aged thirty-seven, born on the second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mingdao, his grandfather Zhichang, his father Pu, a Prefectural School Professor, and his mother née Ni; both parents were living. His elder brother was Song. He married a woman née Xia. He placed eighty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 300th in the Metropolitan Examination.

An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had an illegible courtesy name (□□) and birth order (□); he was forty-one, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bangxian; his grandfather, Sigong; his father, Zhen, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Renshu and Ren’en, and his younger brother was Renyu. His wife was née Wang. He ranked thirty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Hong 周洪 was registered in an artisan household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Tinggao and was first in birth order; he was thirty-seven, born on the eleventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zonggui; his grandfather, Jingzhong; his father, Lin; his mother, née Fan; and his stepmother, née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Ze, Ji, Pu, Hao, Run, and Lin. His wife was née Wei. He ranked one hundred thirteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Liang 陳亮 was registered in a civilian household in Guangde Subprefecture, in the directly administered region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Zhiming and was fourth in birth order; he was twenty-nine, born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather, Hui; his father, Shu; his mother, née Zhao; and his stepmother, née Yan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ji, Ying, and Yan, and his younger brothers were Ze, Chun, Han, Hao, and Zhang. His wife was née Hu. He ranked twenty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Tingyu and was second in birth order; he was thirty-five, born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His elder brothers were Xin and another whose name is illegible (□) [?], and his younger brother was Jin. His wife was née Liang. translation_en:
Gao Tan, registered in a civilian household in □□ County [?], Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Lüdao; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zihe, his grandfather Weichu, and his father Jingyang; his mother was née Chen, and his stepmothers were née Fang and née Chen. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Lin. He ranked third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Wen, registered in a civilian household in Jinzhou, Hanzhong Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Daoxian; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the eleventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Kui, his grandfather Cheng, and his father Hong, an official awaiting selection for appointment; his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Wu. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked forty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang He, registered in a civilian household in Qian'an County, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yijie; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jingxian, his grandfather Bin, and his father Zheng, a Police Chief; his mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Cong and Rong. He married a woman née Gao and subsequently a woman née Ma. He ranked seventy-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Rui, registered in a salt-producing household in Anyi County, Jiezhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the school attached to the Hedong Salt Distribution Commission, specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Wenqing; he was third in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Juyi, his grandfather Yuanji, honorifically granted the title of Investigating Censor, and his father Lian, a Prefect; his mother was née Yi, honorifically granted the title of Lady (ruren). His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brothers were Long and Kui, and his younger brothers were □ [?], Han, Xuan, Li, Wen, Cai, and Ye. He married a woman whose surname is illegible (□). He ranked second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
□ Yi, courtesy name Boju, was registered with the Daning Central Guard under a military registration [?; three characters illegible]. He was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. The wording concerning his birth order and age is garbled, apparently giving his age as thirty-three [?]; he was born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongfu, his grandfather Keming, his father Wenxin, and his mother née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Mo. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Ge. He placed sixty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Kuan, courtesy name Ruli, held civilian registration in Qian’an County, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered territory. He was an added-quota student of the county school, specializing in the Book of Odes. Second in birth order and aged twenty-five, he was born on the first day [?; one character illegible] of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Renmei, his grandfather Zheng, his father Tong, a prefectural registrar, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Hong and his younger brother Xuan. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed eighty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Gai, courtesy name Guanjie, held civilian registration in Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. He was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. Fourth in birth order and aged thirty-three, he was born on the seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanhai, his grandfather Qiyang, his father Zunxue, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Guan and Xian; his younger brothers were Dian, Fang, Ao, and He. He married a woman née Wang. He placed sixty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 345th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Tingzan, courtesy name Zongjing, held military registration in Guang Prefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan. He was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. Third in birth order and aged thirty-two, he was born on the tenth or a subsequent day [?; 十□] of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing; his grandfather Zhong was posthumously granted the title of assistant minister of a court; his father Jin was Assistant Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud. His mother, née Zhou, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Repose, and his stepmother, née Fang, was granted the same title. His father was deceased and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Tingzhen, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Tingxiu; his younger brothers were Ting□ and Tingpei. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Wang. His rank in the Henan Provincial Examination was thirty-something [?; final character illegible], and he placed 315th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Bao Yu, registered in Guilin Zhong□ [?], Guangxi, belonged to a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Haowen and ranked first among his brothers; his age is garbled in the transcription (言□十) [?], and he was born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Youcai, his grandfather Yong, his father Wen, and his mother née Lu. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Zhen, You, Si, and Qi, and his wife was née Chen. He placed third in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Ming, registered in Changqing County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Tingyao, ranked third among his brothers, and was aged thirty-six, born on the tenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Shixian, his grandfather Si, his father Gui, and his mother née Meng. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Jing, a Guard Registrar, and Zhong; his wife was née Wang. He placed ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Chongwen, registered in Xiangyin County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to an official household. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Tingzhang, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged twenty-three, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather Shimin was a School Instructor, posthumously granted the titles of Junior Guardian, concurrently Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Revenue. His grandfather Yuanji was Junior Guardian, concurrently Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Revenue, with the prestige title of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Special Advancement; he was posthumously granted the title of Grand Preceptor and the name Zhongjing. His father Xuan was Chief Minister of the Office of Imperial Seals. His father's former wife, née Zhou, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Suitability; his mother, née Zhang, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chongwu and Chongxun, and his wife was née Wang. He placed twelfth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Ying, registered in Pengcheng Guard, belonged to an official household and was a native of Xi County, Henan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Wenjun, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-six, born on the tenth day [?] of the tenth month. Jing, whose relationship to him is illegible [?], was a Battalion Commander; his grandfather Quan was also a Battalion Commander. His father was Mian, and his mother was née Shi. The notation concerning his surviving parents is illegible [?]. His younger brother Fang was a Battalion Commander [?], and his wife was née Liang. He placed sixth in the Provincial Examination of an illegible jurisdiction [?] and 192nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gong Hong 龔弘, courtesy name Yuanzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region (Zhili). A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in family birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the eighteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zian, his grandfather Dehua, his father Yu, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Chi, and his wife was née Shen. He placed twenty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ni Jinxian 倪進賢, courtesy name Bingzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region (Zhili). A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was seventh in family birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shi’an, his grandfather Yifu, an Instructor, his father Xi, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His wife was née Wang. He placed 108th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jing 張境, courtesy name Menghui, was registered in a civilian household in Yongfu County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An Assistant Instructor at the county school of Shanyang in the directly administered region (Zhili), he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was second in family birth order, aged forty, and born on the ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weigong, his grandfather Si, a tribute student, his father Duo, an Assistant Instructor, and his mother née Wu. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Ying, and his younger brothers were Xuan, Qi, and Lin. His wife was née Huang. He placed thirty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Da 熊達, courtesy name Chengzhang, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in family birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongming, his grandfather Shixin, his father Xuan, and his mother née Qiu. His father alone was living. His elder brother was Tong, and his wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Xian was from □□ County [?], Ji'an, Jiangxi, registered in a civilian household, and a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name is illegible (□□). He ranked second among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Ruchen; his grandfather, Deyu, received the honorary title of Vice Director; his father, Chang, was a Prefect; and his mother, née Wang, received the title of Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Di, and his younger brothers were □ [?], Shi (a tribute student), and Yun. He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Wen was from Yiwu County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, registered in a civilian household, and a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yunda. He ranked second among his brothers, was aged forty-six, and was born on the twenty-third day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Yi, was an Academician-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy, posthumously granted the title of Academician and the name Zhongwen. His grandfather, Shen, was an Erudite of the Directorate of Education; his father was Tu. His father's principal wife was née Wang, his stepmother was née Wu, and his birth mother was née Xu. His parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yue. He married a woman née Yu. He placed thirty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yuan was from Tong'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, registered in a military household, and a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zijun. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the twenty-first day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Gongfu, his grandfather was Tingji, his father was Yongxin, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yi, Ding, Lian, Yong, and Shu. He married a woman née Chen. He placed eighty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 323rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ming Jing was from Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, registered in a military household, and a Confucian scholar. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhiyong. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xiqing, his grandfather was Tong, his father was Yuzheng, and his mother was née Luo. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Gong. He placed forty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Song Jian, registered in Yangcheng County, Zezhou, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Keming; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two [?], and born on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Sicheng, his grandfather Heng, and his father Xing; his mother was née Ma. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xuan, and his wife was née Ma. He ranked seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Tinghe, registered in Xindu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jiefu; he was first in birth order, aged nineteen, and born on the nineteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Shoushan, his grandfather Wen (a subprefectural clerk), and his father Chun (a tribute scholar, gongshi); his mother was née Ye. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Tingping, Tingyi, Tingjian, and Tingxuan. He was betrothed to a woman née Huang. He ranked seventeenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Niu Tong, registered in Datong County, Datong Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Daoheng; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Dalin, his grandfather Xing, and his father Zhen (a county registrar). His legal mother and birth mother were both née Wang. His parents were deceased. His younger brother was Kui, and his wife was née Li. He ranked tenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 154th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Hong, registered in Anlu Guard, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xifan; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the second day of the intercalary fourth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Rang, and his father Cong; his mother was née Chen and his stepmother née Wu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Hai, Han 漢, Han 瀚, Bian, and Yi, and his wife was née Tang. He ranked sixty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
□□ Teng □□騰, whose name has two illegible characters, was registered in □□ County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Boqi, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged forty-eight, born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guiwu; his grandfather, Mengsheng; his father, Yingxiang; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Shichao, Shuncheng, Shunfu, and Shunxie. He married a woman née Zhu and subsequently a woman née Tang. He placed sixty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Han 宋漢 was registered in Jiaozhou, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Tianzhang, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-two, born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was 𤣱宗 ([?] Zong), posthumously granted the title of Guard Registrar; his grandfather was Bian; and his father, Yi. His father's former wife was née Wang; his mother was née Zheng; and his stepmother, née Xia. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Gui, and his younger brother, Xiu. He married a woman née Ji and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed fiftieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zongli 汪宗禮 was registered in Fanchang County, Taiping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Jingfu, ranked third among his brothers, and was aged thirty-nine, born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing; his grandfather, Sizhi; his father, Run, an official of a River Fisheries Office; and his mother, née Pan. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Zongjing; his younger brothers were Zongqi, Zongfan, Zongwen, and Zongzhang. He married a woman née Wu. He placed seventy-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Rui 陳瑞 was registered in Zhongzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Tinggui, ranked third among his brothers, and was aged thirty-five, born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Renke; his grandfather, Yingrong; his father, Jian; and his mother, née Xiang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Qiong and Ying. He married a woman née Xie. He placed twenty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sun Yin, registered in Qingyuan County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Dehong; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the tenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gancheng; his grandfather, Zi; and his father, Qing, a County Magistrate. His mother was née Zheng, and his stepmother was née Tian. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xuan, an Assistant Instructor, and Ning; his younger brothers were Rong and Zong. His wife was née Zhang. He ranked seventeenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 332nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Lian, registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhichun; he was third in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weinan, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Studs; his grandfather, Binghe, an Instructor; and his father, Yuanhui. His mother was née Tu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Hua, Rui, Tang, Gang, Tong, and Mou. His wife was née Jiang. He ranked eighty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Shi, registered in Shanghe County, Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yixu; he was second in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the twenty-first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui and his grandfather was Xing, each posthumously granted the title of Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left. His father was Min, and his mother was née Gao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Hui. His wife was née Zhang; his subsequent wife was also née Zhang. He ranked forty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Zhang, registered in Xu Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Tinggui; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather, Kai; and his father, An. His mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Heng, and his younger brother was Ji. His wife was née Lu. He ranked fifth in the Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李善〔貫陝西鳳翔府隴州，民籍，州學生，治易經，字宗元，行六，年三十五，四月初六日生〕。曾祖惟中〔贈監察御史〕，祖昇〔按察司副使〕，父溥〔倉大使〕，母馮氏。具慶下，兄温、良、儉、讓、景，弟美、時、用、德、洪，娶閆氏。陝西鄉試第二十七名，會試第一百九名。
translation_en:
Tang 𤆇 [?; given-name reading uncertain], courtesy name Keli, was registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, in a military household. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Congshan, his grandfather Rang, his father Zhi, and his mother née Chen; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Guang, an Instructor, and Hou; his younger brother was Du. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed forty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kang Hou, courtesy name Benchun, was registered in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the sixteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Rong, an Admonisher, his father Xin, an Assistant Instructor, and his mother née Yu; both parents were living. His elder brother was Fu and his younger brother Nian. He married a woman née Fu. He placed thirtieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Chen, courtesy name Jingxun, was registered in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the twenty-third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Minister of Rites, his grandfather Min, his father Gong, and his mother née Xu; both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Kai and Wei, the latter an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Yi and Nao. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed forty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shan, courtesy name Zongyuan, was registered in Longzhou, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household. A subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weizhong, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor, his grandfather Sheng, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, his father Pu, a Granary Commissioner, and his mother née Feng; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wen, Liang, Jian, Rang, and Jing; his younger brothers were Mei, Shi, Yong, De, and Hong. He married a woman née Yan. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

杜桓〔貫富峪衛官籍，江西吉水縣人，國子生，治書經，字公□□，年三十五，二月初二日生〕。曾祖玄德，祖大鵬，父文邦〔指揮〕，母覃氏。慈侍下。弟楷、□。娶鄧氏。順天府鄉試第一百三十□名，會試第三十五名。
translation_en:
Yang Shi, registered in the scholarly category in □□ County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhixin; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-one years old, and was born on the sixteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather Weijing was posthumously granted the title of Vice Minister, subsequently raised to Minister; his grandfather Sen was posthumously granted the title of Compiler and subsequently that of Minister [?]; his father Ding was Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Revenue; and his mother, née Li, was invested with the title of Lady. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shifu, a tribute scholar; Shida, a student of the Directorate of Education; Shishu; and Shixin. He married a woman née Li. He placed thirteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xiang, registered in the military category in Shangshui County, Chenzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Junqing; he ranked third among his brothers, was twenty-five years old, and was born on the twenty-second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather San was posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission; his grandfather Yi held that office; his father Rong was a Magistrate; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chen and Zuo, the latter an Official for Righteousness, and his younger brother was Zhao. He married a woman née Liang and subsequently became betrothed to a woman née Xu. He placed ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 325th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Hao, registered in the military category in Lushi County, Shanzhou, Henan Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Minzhan; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was forty-two years old, and was born on the twenty-first day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was De; his grandfather was Wen; his father Zhong was a Magistrate; and his mother was née Su. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jin, Zhen, and Rui; his younger brothers were Kai, Yue, and Zhao. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Huan, registered in the official category at Fuyu Guard and originally from Jishui County, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name is recorded as Gong□□ [?]; he was thirty-five years old and was born on the second day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xuande; his grandfather was Dapeng; his father Wenbang was a Commander; and his mother was née Tan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers are recorded as Kai and □ [?]. He married a woman née Deng. He placed 130-something [?] in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination—the final digit is illegible—and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

王進，貫應天府上元縣，匠籍，國子生。治書經，字以正，行一，年三十四，九月二十九日生。曾祖二郎，祖志能，父誠，母曹氏。具慶下，弟通、達，娶蔡氏。應天府鄉試第九十八名，會試第二百七十八名。

董豫，貫浙江紹興府會稽縣，軍籍，國子生。治詩經，字惟和，行六，年三十八，四月十九日生。曾祖彦□，祖孚言，父敬〔前典籍〕，母宋氏，繼母季氏。永感下，兄剛、觀，弟復〔知縣〕、艮，娶盛氏。浙江鄉試第三十□□，會試第二百二十一名。
translation_en:
□□ Ning, registered in an illegible locality under Huaiqing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Kong□, and he ranked first among his brothers. His age is partly illegible (□□六) [?]; he was born on the twentieth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Hanren, his grandfather Botai, and his father Wei 〔Instructor〕; his mother was née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Daoning, and he married a woman née Jin. He placed fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Lei, registered in Gui'an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Yuanqi, and he ranked fifth among his brothers. He was thirty-five years old, born on the fourth day of the intercalary twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Dezhang, his grandfather Shineng, and his father Yi; his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Lin, Heng, and Yuan, and he married a woman née Pan. He placed eighty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jin, registered in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yizheng, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Erlang, his grandfather Zhineng, and his father Cheng; his mother was née Cao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tong and Da, and he married a woman née Cai. He placed ninety-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Yu, registered in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weihe, and he ranked sixth among his brothers. He was thirty-eight years old, born on the nineteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yan□, his grandfather Fuyan, and his father Jing 〔formerly Librarian〕; his mother was née Song and his stepmother née Ji. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Gang and Guan; his younger brothers were Fu 〔District Magistrate〕 and Gen. He married a woman née Sheng. His Zhejiang Provincial Examination rank is partly illegible (第三十□□), apparently thirtieth or another rank in the thirties [?]; he placed 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.
